rubric.note: Subjective internal editorial ratings with evidence; not an automatic humour metric or an independent live review.

card.title: Competing Theories
card.instruction: Create several explanations for what is happening. Test each new clue against them, and switch allegiance whenever one theory gains strength.

transfer.action: I move {prop} between two rival explanations on the table.
transfer.opening: Let's test the explanation, not just defend it. {request}
transfer.response: That answer changes which theory gets the next chance. {counter}
transfer.challenge: I thought you'd made up your mind.
transfer.closing: The evidence keeps insisting I leave it somewhere movable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was the missing cake taken, dropped, or eaten by the dog? Describe the crumbs before choosing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on the dog.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dog leads. Were those crumbs present before dinner too?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, after you fed it your slice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then theft returns to contention. Start again with who opened the cupboard.

bespokePairs.seedUse: Competing explanations guide exact evidence questions; new details force A to shift theory rather than stack unconnected accusations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The parcel was lost, stolen, or delivered elsewhere. Was it a bag or a box?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A box with handles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Delivery error leads. Describe the lid.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was tied, not hinged.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then 'box' loses support. Let's establish the container before accusing a driver.

bespokePairs.seedUse: Adapts S144-single-b's competing explanations and changing preference to a missing parcel, using D126-single-a's bag-versus-box, handles and lid inquiry. A1 proposes loss, theft and misdelivery; A3 favors delivery error after B2 describes handles, while A5 uses B4's tied lid to reconsider the container label. The last change concerns classification, not a demonstrated switch among the original disappearance theories. That exact-pair fidelity reservation remains pending; this amendment corrects source attribution without approving the dialogue.

card.title: Competing Theories
card.instruction: Create several explanations for what is happening. Test each new clue against them, and switch allegiance whenever one theory gains strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The missing cake is theft, accident, or the dog. Keep all three on the board.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on the dog.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dog moves into first place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on you too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then theft deserves renewed funding.

card.title: What Really Happened?
card.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was the parcel in a bag or a box? You've used both words.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A bag, I think.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Describe the handles before choosing the noun.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It had a rigid lid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Let's build the object before the story.

card.title: Competing Theories
card.instruction: Create several explanations for what is happening. Test each new clue against them, and switch allegiance whenever one theory gains strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The lights failed because of weather, wiring, or the caretaker's shortcut.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's sunny.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Weather withdraws gracefully.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The caretaker unplugged them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Shortcut wins. Wiring can keep its dignity.

card.title: What Really Happened?
card.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me again what happened between four and four-ten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already explained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it should match one of these two versions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stopped for coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Where does coffee fit into the version with the bus?

card.title: Competing Theories
card.instruction: Create several explanations for what is happening. Test each new clue against them, and switch allegiance whenever one theory gains strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our wedding cake's gone: theft, accident, or the dog. I suspect theft.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on him. Get him outside before Mum sees.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dog leads. I'll take him; check under the table for crumbs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That icing's from yesterday. The crumbs lead into the cloakroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Theft leads again. Keep the dog here; let's see whether that trail ends at a dropped cake or somebody's coat.

card.title: Competing Theories
card.instruction: Create several explanations for what is happening. Test each new clue against them, and switch allegiance whenever one theory gains strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The hall lights failed: weather, wiring, or the caretaker saving electricity. Wiring's my favourite.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He unplugged them. Help me reach the socket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Economy takes the lead. I'll hold your ladder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The socket's wet. There's rain coming through the roof.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Weather overtakes him. Leave the plug; let's ask whether he unplugged it before the leak.
